analysis.title: FX Daily: Defensive rotation in play
key_insights: ING sees a subtle regime shift: higher energy prices no longer mean 'higher rates forever', and the long end is expressing more worry about growth.
Defensive rotation appears underway into the Swiss franc, the yen and sterling as the US midterms approach.

Global equity investors may be scaling back tech exposure for defensives such as consumer staples, healthcare and utilities, which would favour European equities because their benchmark tech weights are lower.
A Democrat sweep of Congress in the early November US midterms could slow or reverse deregulation.
The 1-month USD OIS priced 10 years forward fell from 5.17% to 4.85% as yield curves flattened, against a neutral rate near 3.50%.
ING expects defensive currencies to outperform commodity currencies, but says the dollar has no case to fall across the board until the short end of the US curve buckles.
ING favours consolidation over correction for DXY, with possible softening to the 101.25/30 area. The US data calendar is light, so the dollar is expected to follow tech stocks.
EUR/USD is holding up despite higher energy prices and the unresolved French budget crisis. ING attributes this to a gentle unwinding of concentrated positioning in US tech and the dollar.

Fed tightening expectations have stayed at about +75bp for weeks. ING thinks that can persist and keep the dollar strong, but a tech wobble that causes dovish repricing at the short end could trigger a broader dollar correction.
ING expects sterling to hold gains because of market confidence in a Bank of England tightening cycle (25bp hikes in February and November), which makes it a high-carry European currency.
EUR/GBP is expected to stay in a 0.8360-0.8430 range after breaking below 0.8400. The UK budget next week is seen as unlikely to derail this, and French politics leave the euro room to fall.

ING expects the Central Bank of Turkey to cut rates by 100bp to 36.00% today, resuming easing for the first time since the US-Iran conflict began, with another 100bp cut in December to 35% by year-end.
The carry trade in TRY is expected to continue despite crowded long positions, with USD/TRY forecast at 51.50 by year-end.

sector_views.rationale: Global equity investors are suspected to be rotating out of tech into these defensive sectors.
Tech stocks remain fragile as investors digest Meta and Tesla Q3 results and what they imply for capex plans, and exposure is suspected to be scaling back.
Lower tech weights in benchmark indices favour a geographic allocation shift toward Europe.

earnings_insights: Meta and Tesla Q3 results and their implications for capex plans are still being digested by the market, with no figures given in this report.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 5.17% in late summer and September, though still well above a neutral rate near 3.50%. Curve flattening suggests more worry about growth than inflation.
Reference point against which the forward OIS pricing is judged.
Market pricing has been stable for weeks. ING thinks it can remain so, which supports the dollar.

macro_indicators.indicator: Central Bank of Turkey policy rate
macro_indicators.interpretation: The cut resumes easing. ING expects another 100bp in December, taking the rate to 35% by year-end.
ING's forecast, well below the policy rate, so real rates stay high and the carry trade remains attractive.
The expected tightening cycle makes sterling a high-carry European currency.

risk_factors: A tech selloff that prompts a dovish repricing at the short end of the US curve, leading to a broader dollar correction.
Persistent energy prices and attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The French budget crisis weighing on the euro.
Counterparty exposures from the Turkish investment fund shock remain the main spillover risk, and tighter liquidity could weaken domestic demand.
The US midterms, with a possible Democrat sweep slowing or reversing deregulation.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning in US tech and the dollar is heavy and concentrated, and it is being gently pared back.
Crowded long TRY positions offer less and less carry but remain popular in emerging markets.
A dovish repricing at the short end of the US curve after a tech wobble is the identified trigger for a broader dollar correction.
geopolitical: Attacks against Saudi Arabia continue and keep a hefty risk premium in oil prices.
The US-Iran conflict paused the Central Bank of Turkey's easing cycle.
The unresolved French budget crisis is weighing on the euro.
The US midterms in early November could produce a Democrat sweep of Congress.

tension_points.bull_case: Fed tightening expectations of about +75bp have stayed rock-solid, the short end of the US curve is firm, and positioning favours continued dollar strength.
tension_points.bear_case: A tech wobble that prompts dovish repricing at the short end could lead to a broader dollar correction, and defensive currencies are rotating higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The short end of the US yield curve starting to buckle.
